name: nethack
why: A legendary roguelike with deep emergent systems, though it is a famous default among terminal game players.

brief.what_it_is: NetHack is a single-player roguelike video game that runs in a terminal, as its Homebrew description states. The homepage describes it as the long-running home of the game, with downloadable binaries for Windows, Amiga, and MS-DOS and a version 5.0.0 release dated 2026-05-02. The homepage text does not describe gameplay, controls, or what the player sees, so the mechanics here come from the Homebrew description and the scout notes, not from the page I read. The homepage's emphasis is on the project's history, community, and release announcements.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no explicit reason for existing beyond being the official home of NetHack and its releases. Its framing is playful: "Congratulations adventurer! Your quest is at an end for you have reached the home of NetHack."
brief.install_notes: The homepage links to binaries for Windows, Amiga, and MS-DOS, with updated builds posted in June 2026. It mentions Ingo Paschke's Amiga port for 5.0.0 and his work on an Atari port (and possibly a Motorola 68000 Mac port) on a GitHub branch, and says volunteers are wanted to test and cross-compile it. The homepage does not mention Homebrew, a Unix build, or any runtime, account, or configuration step, so I could not confirm install steps beyond the brew formula name and the executable name nethack from the metadata.
brief.standout: The site is unusually heavy on history: a long list of press, academic papers (including an IEEE Spectrum piece and an IEEE/NASA software archaeology paper), comic strips, and quotes spanning decades. The Homebrew scout notes call it a famous default among terminal game players, but the homepage itself does not make that claim in those words.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage lists NetHack 5.0.0 released on 2026-05-02, with binary updates for Windows, Amiga, and MS-DOS through 2026-06-09, and a 2026-05-22 note about an active Atari port effort.
brief.caveats: I read only the homepage, which is not a GitHub repository, so there was no README to read. The page does not describe features, platform support for Homebrew, or licensing. Some of the links in the page's reference list are served from archive.org, as the page itself notes. The homepage also says the website is starting a long journey to add accessibility functionality, which suggests accessibility is still in progress.
quotes: Congratulations adventurer! Your quest is at an end for you have reached the home of NetHack.
Within, the Wizard of Yendor has no power, the Oracle speaks with utmost clarity, and the grid bugs do not bite.
In short, NetHack 3.1.3 is the most elaborate role-playing environment you are ever likely to explore.
fetch_log: https://www.nethack.org/ — fetched OK; homepage text read, announcements and references included; no README since it is not a GitHub repo
